subtitle: A Widow, a Kingdom, and the Path of the Dharma

panels.shot: wide, low-angle tableau of a forest hermitage clearing with a dim, unlit pyre in the foreground and Rajyashri standing firm beside it, robes stirred by wind
panels.action: Rajyashri stands at the edge of an unlit pyre in a shadowed Vindhya forest clearing, chin raised, as distant hermit huts and dark trees frame her like a silent court.

dialogue.text: In the age when Kannauj was a prize for kings, Rajyashri stood before a fire she would not enter, and chose a different throne.

i18n.hi: जब कन्नौज राजाओं की सबसे बड़ी लूट था, राज्यश्री उस आग के सामने खड़ी थी जिसमें वो नहीं कूदी… और उसने दूसरा सिंहासन चुन लिया।

panels.shot: medium close-up, straight-on, with faint superimposed silhouettes of two kingdoms behind her
panels.action: A young Rajyashri, adorned as a princess, stands between faint, looming outlines of Sthanvishvara’s palace and Kannauj’s city walls, as if her small figure is the bridge between them.

dialogue.text: She was born Rajyashri of Sthanvishvara, a princess whose marriage would tie two northern thrones: her father’s Pushyabhuti house and the Maukhari kings of Kannauj.

i18n.hi: वो स्थान्विष्‍वर की राजकुमारी राज्यश्री थी, जिसकी शादी उत्तरी भारत की दो गादियाँ जोड़ने वाली थी — पिता का पुष्यभूति घराना और कन्नौज के मौखरी राजा।

panels.shot: wide ceremonial shot, high balcony view over a royal marriage procession entering Kannauj
panels.action: Rajyashri rides in a covered palanquin amid elephants and banners as she enters the bustling city of Kannauj for her marriage to King Grahavarman, with citizens lining the streets.

dialogue.text: Banabhatta tells us she entered Kannauj as Grahavarman’s bride, a political tie woven with garlands, sealing an alliance between ancient rivals.

i18n.hi: बाणभट्ट लिखते हैं, वो ग्रहवर्मन की दुल्हन बनकर कन्नौज में उतरी — माला‑जोड़ सियासी गठजोड़, जो पुराने दुश्मनों को एक डोर में बाँध गया।

panels.shot: intimate interior, three-quarter view, soft light from a lattice window
panels.action: Inside a Kannauj palace chamber, Rajyashri stands by a carved window, looking out over the city with a calm, thoughtful expression, a small votive lamp beside her.

dialogue.text: For a brief span, she was queen in a city that had outlived many dynasties. The chronicles fall silent here, but in that silence lay her small island of ordinary days.

i18n.hi: थोड़े समय के लिए वो उस शहर की रानी बनी, जो कितनी ही वंशों से बचा रहा था। राजग्रंथ यहाँ चुप हो जाते हैं, पर उसी चुप्पी में उसके कुछ साधारण दिन छुपे हैं।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot, tilted angle, palace courtyard with looming shadow of an invading force beyond the gate
panels.action: Rajyashri stands in a palace courtyard as distant war banners and armored figures of Devagupta’s Malwa forces appear at the broken outer gate, dust rising in the background.

dialogue.text: Then Devagupta of Malwa struck. Bana names him as the usurper who broke Kannauj, killed Grahavarman, and cast Rajyashri into chains.

i18n.hi: फिर मालवा के देवगुप्त ने वार किया। बाण उसे वही गद्दार कहते हैं जिसने कन्नौज तोड़ा, ग्रहवर्मन को मारा, और राज्यश्री को बेड़ियों में जकड़ दिया।

panels.shot: tight interior shot through iron bars, close-up on her face in profile
panels.action: Seen through the bars of a dim cell, Rajyashri sits upright on a bare stone bench, her hair loosened, gaze steady, as light from a high slit traces a bar across her face.

dialogue.text: Harshacharita paints her as the suffering queen in prison, a symbol of outrage to her brothers. Yet behind Bana’s flourish, there is a woman in a dark room, waiting.

i18n.hi: हर्षचरित में वो कारागार की पीड़ित रानी है, भाइयों के क्रोध का प्रतीक। पर बाण की सजावट के पीछे, एक अँधेरे कोठरी में बैठी स्त्री है… जो बस इंतज़ार कर रही है।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot, with ghostly overlays of battles and a funeral pyre behind her
panels.action: Rajyashri’s still figure in the cell foreground; faint behind her, stylized scenes of battle and a royal cremation suggest Rajyavardhana’s march, his death, and the spreading smoke of pyres.

dialogue.text: Her elder brother Rajyavardhana marched to avenge her. He fell in turn. The record gives no voice from her cell, but his death turned her captivity into utter ruin.

i18n.hi: बड़ा भाई राज्यवर्धन उसे छुड़ाने निकला। वो भी मारा गया। इतिहास उसकी कोठरी की आवाज़ नहीं लिखता, पर उसी मौत ने उसकी कैद को पूरी तबाही बना दिया।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot, corridor perspective, with her moving toward an unseen exit
panels.action: Rajyashri, in plain but dignified dress, slips along a shadowed corridor with one attendant behind her, moving toward a distant patch of daylight that hints at freedom.

dialogue.text: After that, Bana tells us, she fled. How she broke free he does not say. Only that she turned away from courts and headed south, toward the Vindhya forests.

i18n.hi: बाण के मुताबिक, इसके बाद वो भाग निकली। कैसे बेड़ियाँ तोड़ीं, ये वो नहीं बताते। बस इतना कि उसने दरबारों से मुँह मोड़ा और दक्षिण की ओर, विन्ध्य के जंगलों की राह ली।

panels.shot: broad landscape shot, slightly elevated, showing a small caravan entering thick forest hills
panels.action: Rajyashri walks with a small group along a narrow path into the Vindhya hills, towering dark trees and creepers closing behind them, a city’s silhouette fading far in the background.

dialogue.text: The Vindhyas, that ancient wall of stone and forest. Banabhatta frames them as a stage set for despair; the path she took turned their hermitages into a shelter from war.

i18n.hi: विन्ध्य — पत्थर और जंगल की पुरानी दीवार। बाण इन्हें निराशा का रंगमंच बनाते हैं, पर जिस राह से वो गई, वही आश्रम युद्ध से बचने की शरण बन गए।

panels.shot: serene wide shot, low angle, forest hermitage with monks and ascetics about
panels.action: In a clearing among tall trees, Rajyashri stands at the edge of a simple hermitage: thatched huts, a small stupa, saffron-robed monks and matted-haired ascetics sharing the same quiet space.

dialogue.text: We are told she reached a forest hermitage, a place where Brahmanical ascetics and Buddhist monks often shared the same groves, while kingdoms tore at each other beyond the trees.

i18n.hi: कहा जाता है, वो एक वनाश्रम पहुँची — जहाँ ब्राह्मण संन्यासी और बौद्ध भिक्षु एक ही उपवन बाँटते थे, जब पेड़ों के बाहर राज्य एक‑दूसरे को नोच रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on her hands near stacked firewood, with an unlit pyre structure visible
panels.action: Rajyashri stands near a carefully stacked pile of firewood in the clearing, her hand hovering over its rough surface, a small clay lamp resting unlit on a stone beside it.

dialogue.text: Here Bana’s courtly art swells. He shows her at the edge of a pyre, resolved to follow her husband into fire. It is drama, not a stenographer’s note.

i18n.hi: यहीं बाण का दरबारी शिल्प चरम पर है। वो उसे चिता के किनारे खड़ा दिखाते हैं, पति के पीछे आग में उतरने को तैयार। ये नाटक है, न कि अदालत की कार्यवाही।

panels.shot: close-up on her face, three-quarter view, eyes distant, with the pyre blurred in the foreground
panels.action: Rajyashri’s face fills the frame, the wooden pyre blurred at the bottom edge; her eyes look past it, full of sorrow but also a searching, unresolved question.

dialogue.text: Modern historians warn us: this near-sati is literature. Yet even as art, it shows her poised on a choice—whether to let a usurper’s crime dictate her final act.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार चेताते हैं: ये लगभग‑सती बस साहित्य है। फिर भी कहानी में वो एक मोड़ पर खड़ी है — क्या गद्दार का जुर्म ही उसकी आख़िरी सांस लिखेगा या नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot, side view, with a Buddhist monk gently speaking to her, forest in the background
panels.action: A calm, elderly Buddhist monk stands beside Rajyashri, hands folded, speaking softly as he gestures away from the pyre toward the hermitage path; she listens, shoulders bowed but not broken.

dialogue.text: Bana gives this speech to her brother; the forest itself might have offered it. There were teachers here who spoke of suffering, and of paths that did not end in flames.

i18n.hi: ये वाक्य बाण ने भाई के मुँह से कहलाया, पर ये खुद जंगल भी कह सकता था। यहाँ गुरु थे, जो दुख और ऐसे रास्तों की बात करते थे जो आग पर ख़त्म नहीं होते।

panels.shot: symbolic close shot of her hand pushing the clay lamp away from the pyre
panels.action: In a tight focus, Rajyashri’s hand moves the small clay lamp away from the stacked wood, setting it instead on the ground facing the path back toward the hermitage huts.

dialogue.text: In Bana’s telling, Harsha rushes in and pulls her back. Whether he found her at the very brink or earlier, the outcome is plain: she stepped away from the fire.

i18n.hi: बाण के अनुसार, हर्षा दौड़कर आता है और उसे खींच लेता है। वो सच में चिता की धार पर थी या उससे पहले, जो भी हो — नतीजा साफ है, वो आग से पीछे हट गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of the clearing, with the unlit pyre receding while she walks toward the hermitage with measured steps
panels.action: Rajyashri walks away from the unused pyre toward the hermitage, back straight, a shawl drawn around her; the abandoned woodpile stands behind her like a muted monument.

dialogue.speaker: rajyashri
dialogue.text: My grief is mine to carry, not theirs to consume.

i18n.hi: मेरा शोक मेरा है, उनकी भूख नहीं।

panels.shot: interior hermitage medium shot, she sits before a monk receiving simple robes
panels.action: Inside a modest hermitage hall, Rajyashri kneels before a Buddhist monk who offers her a folded yellow robe; her royal jewelry lies set aside on a low wooden tray.

dialogue.text: Xuanzang’s careful record, written decades later, speaks of Harsha’s sister as a devoted Buddhist. Somewhere between the prison and this hall, she chose the robe over the crown.

i18n.hi: कई दशक बाद, ह्वेनसांग की सावधान कलम हर्ष की बहन को गहरे बौद्ध रूप में दर्ज करती है। कहीं कारागार और इस सभा के बीच, उसने मुकुट छोड़ वस्त्र चुन लिए।

panels.shot: medium shot, frontal, as she dons the robe, faint outline of a diadem behind her
panels.action: Rajyashri, now in simple Buddhist robes, ties the cloth firmly around her shoulders; behind her, a faint, out-of-focus royal diadem rests on a shelf, half in shadow.

dialogue.text: Harsha would rule from Kannauj, presiding over grand assemblies and patronizing many creeds. His sister stood there too, not as a pawn in his story, but as a practitioner in her own.

i18n.hi: हर्ष कन्नौज से राज करेगा — महा सभाएँ, अनेक मतों का संरक्षण। उसकी बहन भी वहीं खड़ी होगी, मोहरे की तरह नहीं, अपनी साधना की नायिका बनकर।

panels.shot: grand hall wide shot, Harsha’s court in session with her seated among Buddhist elders (Harsha not in cast list so shown indistinct)
panels.action: In a vast audience hall, rows of monks and scholars sit before a distant, indistinct royal figure; among them, Rajyashri sits in her robe, listening intently, a palm-leaf manuscript in her lap.

dialogue.text: Xuanzang saw her at Harsha’s assemblies, as much a part of the religious life of the court as its kings and ministers were of its politics.

i18n.hi: ह्वेनसांग ने उसे हर्ष की सभाओं में देखा — दरबार की धार्मिक धड़कन में उतनी ही शामिल, जितने राजा‑मंत्री राजनीति में।

panels.shot: quiet close-up, older Rajyashri in profile, reading a manuscript by lamplight
panels.action: An older Rajyashri, serene, reads a palm-leaf manuscript by the warm light of an oil lamp, the sounds of the court dim beyond a latticed screen.

dialogue.text: Her story survives in fragments: a court panegyrist’s flourish, a monk’s matter-of-fact note. Between them lies a woman who was traded in alliance, taken in war, and finally chose her own ending.

i18n.hi: उसकी कथा टुकड़ों में बची है — दरबारी गुणगान की चकाचौंध, और एक भिक्षु की सादी टिप्‍पणी। इन दोनों के बीच वो स्त्री है जिसे कभी सौदे में दे दिया गया, युद्ध में छीन लिया गया, और जिसने अंत में अपने अंत पर खुद मुहर लगाई।

title_i18n.en: Rajyashri and the Fire She Refused
title_i18n.hi: राज्यश्री और आग जिसे उसने ठुकराया

subtitle_i18n.en: A Widow, a Kingdom, and the Path of the Dharma
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक विधवा, एक राज्य, और धर्म का रास्ता
